correctness.rationale: Exact semantic-radius lemma proved by induction on the finite approximant, matching necessity by a one-atom countervaluation at a diameter witness; an n-1 geodesic uses every vertex and forbids every chord. Each agent equivalence class in a path has size at most two; matching edge colors are necessary/sufficient, producing a bijection with no overcount. A binomial transfer counts the words. The B^2 positivity and Perron asymptotic were checked. checker.py independently exhausts 7,108 small frame tuples, 234,098 approximant truth-set operations, and 18 independent word counts; finite verification is not the general proof.

value.rationale: A natural finite-model resource measure—uniform iterations needed to compute common knowledge—has an exact global maximum, and this theorem identifies and counts all structures saturating it for arbitrary numbers of agents. The nontrivial S5 equivalence transitivity constraint forces disjoint neighbor edge color sets and yields a finite-state transfer and asymptotic enumeration; this is more informative than the routine diameter bound or isolated examples, and provides a reproducible benchmark for worst-case epistemic-frame instances.
